question.text: Oxidation states of the metal in the minerals haematite and magnetite, respectively, are

options.text: II, III in haematite and III in magnetite
II, III in haematite and II in magnetite
II in haematite and II, III in magnetite
III in haematite and II, III in magnetite

solution.text: Haematite is $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$, in which oxidation number of iron is III. Magnetite is $\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4$ which is infact a mixed oxide (FeO $\cdot \mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ ) hence, iron is present in both II and III oxidation state.
